text:
maria: Quick check — ran into a client that sends X-Org: org-123 but no Authorization header and it also sends x-api-key: old-key. The service returned 401. Is that expected or should we try to resolve by API key and return 403 if unauthorized?

vikram: short answer: we should prefer API key resolution if Authorization is absent. 401 implies missing credentials, 403 implies credentials present but not allowed. So 401 seems misleading here.

maria: hmm ok. The client is a legacy mobile app that we told to rotate keys next week. They might be hitting an old key during graceful overlap. How do we want to behave for multi-key requests? e.g., both Authorization (Bearer new) + x-api-key (old) present.

olivia: Preference is: 1) prefer Authorization bearer token for user-scoped auth, 2) fallback to x-api-key when bearer missing, 3) if both present, trust bearer. That keeps newer clients safer.

kevin: +1. Also need to decide about org/project scoping when only X-Org present. Currently our resolver tries: Authorization -> x-api-key -> X-Org implied org fallback. But for legacy clients with X-Org + invalid key we should not silently accept X-Org alone unless the request came from an internal trusted proxy.

maria: Right. The problematic case: client sends X-Org: org-123 and x-api-key: old-key (expired). The auth flow returned 401 and we showed a generic "missing or invalid credentials" error to the client. Product asked for clearer behavior that helps debugging.

vikram: Proposal: change mapping to these response codes: - no credentials at all -> 401 + hint to include Authorization or x-api-key. - credentials present but failed validation -> 401 if format/crypto invalid, 403 if valid key but not mapped to requested project/org. For fallback-only X-Org acceptance: only in inbound-proxy mode.

olivia: That is reasonable. One nit: "valid key but not mapped" vs "expired key". Expired keys are still validated but rejected — treat as 401 (credential invalid) not 403. 403 should be reserved for authz (key is valid but doesn't have access to target project/org).

kevin: Agree. So mapping table we can summarize in the contract doc and update SDKs. Also need to ensure telemetry: logs should include which signal triggered resolution (e.g., auth=Bearer|x-api-key|x-org-fallback) so we can debug quick.

maria: I captured that. Example responses to document: 
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "invalid_credentials",
  "hint": "include Authorization: Bearer <token> or x-api-key"
}
```
and
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "insufficient_scope",
  "hint": "key or token does not have access to project/route"
}
```

vikram: Also add an X-Auth-Resolution header in responses for internal debugging: X-Auth-Resolution: bearer|api_key|org_fallback|none. Keep it off by default for public prod but enabled behind a logging flag so SRE can toggle.

infra-bot: deploy/beta-auth-telemetry to staging scheduled at 2026-03-18T02:00Z :rocket:

olivia: One more edge: key rotation grace window. We currently accept rotated keys for 10 minutes after rotation to allow rollouts. Document that as: rotated keys accepted for 10m if rotation event has "grace": true and request includes x-api-key or Authorization matching new key. Otherwise expired -> 401.

maria: Thanks — I'll update the API contract PR with the decision and examples, plus a small note for SDK authors to prefer Authorization when present. I'll also add the telemetry header behind the feature flag.

kevin: Ping me on the PR for a quick review. If we can include tests for each response case (no creds, invalid, expired, valid-no-access, valid-access) that'd be great.

maria: Will do. Thanks everyone :heart:
